The named paper is not among the permanent documents, and no competing session paper is indicated; I’ll check the session knowledge scope first, then search the web if needed.
```python
paper_knowledge = await knowledge_search_knowledge("Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish Dragon Diet fish bag volume", scope="session")
print(paper_knowledge)
```
The knowledge search did not provide the paper’s calculation, so I’ll search the public web for the paper and the specific fish-bag volume.
```python
paper_web_search = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon\'s Diet?" fish bag volume m3', max_results=5)
print(paper_web_search)
```
The search results identify the paper; I’ll retrieve the source text or PDF details to verify the exact calculated value rather than infer it.
I’ll inspect the returned search entries for a direct paper URL, then fetch that source.
```python
paper_search_preview = paper_web_search
print(paper_search_preview)
```
The search response needs a more targeted source lookup; I’ll search for the paper title on the University of Leicester domain and related copies.
```python
leicester_search = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish" University of Leicester PDF', max_results=10)
print(leicester_search)
```
I’ll broaden the lookup to indexed copies and repositories, where the paper’s PDF or text may expose the calculation directly.
```python
repository_search = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish" PDF dragon diet', max_results=10)
print(repository_search)
```
I’ll query the distinctive phrase together with “bag” and “volume” to surface the numerical passage directly.
```python
volume_search = await web_search('"Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish" "bag" volume', max_results=10)
print(volume_search)
```
I’ll run one final exact-number-oriented search for the unit and title, which should return the relevant calculation if it is indexed.
```python
exact_unit_search = await web_search('"Hiccup" "fish bag" "m^3"', max_results=10)
print(exact_unit_search)
```
The search tool is not exposing the result text reliably, so I’ll query the public search endpoint from the sandbox and extract the paper links/snippets.
```python
search_html = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s 'https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q=%22Can+Hiccup+Supply+Enough+Fish%22' | sed -n '1,160p'")
print(search_html)
```
I’ll use a direct HTML search for the distinctive title plus the likely unit, then inspect the returned snippets.
```python
unit_html = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s 'https://html.duckduckgo.com/html/?q=%22Can+Hiccup+Supply+Enough+Fish%22+%22m%5E3%22' | sed -n '1,220p'")
print(unit_html)
```
I’ll retrieve only the result URLs and titles from the search HTML to locate the University of Leicester document.
```python
links_html = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s 'https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Can+Hiccup+Supply+Enough+Fish%22' | grep -oE 'https?[^&\" ]+' | head -30")
print(links_html)
```
I’ll query Bing’s RSS endpoint, which returns compact, parseable snippets for this title.
```python
bing_rss = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s 'https://www.bing.com/search?format=rss&q=%22Can+Hiccup+Supply+Enough+Fish%22' | sed -n '1,240p'")
print(bing_rss)
```
I’ll query Crossref for the exact title to identify the article record and its downloadable source.
```python
crossref_title = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s --get 'https://api.crossref.org/works' --data-urlencode 'query.title=Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon’s Diet' --data-urlencode 'rows=5' | sed -n '1,120p'")
print(crossref_title)
```
I’ll check an academic index for the paper’s abstract/full-text link.
```python
semantic_lookup = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s --get 'https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search' --data-urlencode 'query=Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon Diet' --data-urlencode 'limit=5' --data-urlencode 'fields=title,url,openAccessPdf,abstract' | sed -n '1,160p'")
print(semantic_lookup)
```
I’ll search for the paper’s wording around the result, specifically the sentence likely containing the fish-bag volume.
```python
sentence_search = await web_search('"fish bag" "dragon\'s diet" volume', max_results=10)
print(sentence_search)
```
I’ll use OpenAlex’s title search as another route to the indexed paper and its landing page.
```python
openalex_lookup = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s --get 'https://api.openalex.org/works' --data-urlencode 'search=Can Hiccup Supply Enough Fish to Maintain a Dragon Diet' --data-urlencode 'per-page=5' | sed -n '1,180p'")
print(openalex_lookup)
```
I’ll check whether the paper is mirrored in Leicester’s journal archive under a downloadable PDF path.
```python
archive_search = await run_command("curl -L --max-time 20 -s 'https://www.google.com/search?q=site%3Awww2.le.ac.uk%2Fprojects%2Fjist+%22Hiccup%22+fish' | grep -oE '.{0,120}(Hiccup|hiccup).{0,200}' | head -20")
print(archive_search)
```
I’ll extract any PDF or article URLs returned by the searches so the source can be checked directly.
```python
url_candidates = []
for source in [paper_web_search, leicester_search, repository_search, volume_search, exact_unit_search]:
    if isinstance(source, dict):
        stack = [source]
    elif isinstance(source, list):
        stack = list(source)
    else:
        stack = [source]
    while stack:
        item = stack.pop()
        if isinstance(item, dict):
            stack.extend(item.values())
        elif isinstance(item, list):
            stack.extend(item)
        elif isinstance(item, str) and ("http" in item or ".pdf" in item):
            url_candidates.append(item)
print(url_candidates[:20])
```
